lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Donna, it's Daniela from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, not much. I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, my health is why I'm doing this. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walking fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're giving everything to work right now, and there's not much left over for you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I've been watching my grandkids all week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're so used to looking after other people that it's hard to make room for yourself.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. My knees have been bothering me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the pain gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Donna. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Daniela. Bye!

flags.reason: Participant asked to move the call later (line 30); coach did not acknowledge or confirm the change.
Closed question about the mall ignores the participant's stated plan and guilt; the mall was never raised before, so it feels off-track.

score.summary: Daniela used mostly reflections and open questions that drew out Donna's change talk around the 20-minute walk and her backup plan. She missed Donna's request to reschedule the call and asked a closed mall question that did not follow from what Donna had said.
strengths: Line 11 and 13: complex reflections drew out Donna's desire to keep moving and fit walking into real life.
Line 27: open question about a backup plan ("what's your backup plan?") led to a concrete hallway option in line 28.
Line 21: affirmed Donna's follow-through, which she accepted in line 22.
coaching_tips: Line 30: acknowledge the reschedule request and confirm a new time before closing.
Line 17: ask about the mall only after checking what Donna is planning; try an open question such as "What feels doable for you this week?"
Line 19 and 9: good reflections; add a feelings check on her guilt (line 6) before moving to a goal.
Line 29: summarize the plan (early 20-minute walk, hallway backup) before setting next contact.
